text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove repeated logic. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after the changes. It is important because it helps reduce technical debt, which builds up over time when code is written quickly. By refactoring regularly, developers keep their projects clean, flexible, and easier for the whole team to work with.
